original_test_intent: Run the supported DCGM level-4 diagnostic with the denylist scope active and determine from complete per-subtest output whether any GPU is excluded or any diagnostic fails.
original_method: Pin DCGM/driver/GPU compatibility and denylist definition; capture persistence/service/workload and health baselines; preserve logs; start the service in supported order, enable approved persistence state, run one full level-4 diagnostic under isolation and monitoring, retain all subtests, then restore the approved runtime state.
manual_activity: GPU diagnostics owner approves the DCGM release, denylist policy, level-4 scope, runtime/stop limits and final persistence/service state; operator isolates workloads and monitors the SUT.
required_inputs: Authoritative denylist configuration and level-4 subtest map
Maintenance window, OOB and workload isolation
safety_requirements: Do not expose credentials or bypass host identity
Preserve complete output and pre/post logs
Start services only in documented order
Monitor GPU, thermal, power and host health
Stop on fault and do not retry automatically
agent_execution_scope: Validate DCGM compatibility, denylist scope and approval
Capture baseline and start supported runtime state
Map every subtest and denylist result
Restore approved state and report without DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve diagnostic level/order and denylist oracle
Approve disruptive run and stop limits

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It reorders the service more plausibly but conflicts with its own level-1 evidence instruction, exposes credentials, disables host verification and truncates the required level-4 result.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Start the approved service through authenticated access, set persistence only after approval, then capture full `dcgmi diag -v -r 4` output without a tail filter.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Level 4, 120-minute machine allowance, persistence change and full diagnostic acceptance are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind each returned level-4 subtest and denylist/exclusion indication to the complete raw run, telemetry and explicit acceptance matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects service sequencing and adds complete evidence, security, state restoration and safety monitoring.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A level-1 sanity run or last 30 lines cannot establish the source's level-4 denylist result.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Level-4 diagnostics may load GPUs, affect workloads and expose latent faults.

project_override_considerations: The project must define whether any denylisted GPU is an automatic BLOCKED/FAIL condition or an authorized exclusion and list the expected subtests for this platform.
expected_evidence: Full level-4 command, exit and per-subtest results
Restored runtime state and engineer verdict

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row352 Wistron-NV GPU-00345-V002: approve DCGM release and Denylist definition/subtest oracle, service-versus-diagnostic order, source level-4 scope over DeepSeek level-1 evidence, persistence/final-state policy, 120-minute monitoring/abort limits and handling of excluded GPUs; preserve full logs.

review_improvement: Makes the named denylist coverage observable per GPU and subtest while eliminating credential exposure and output truncation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A diagnostic can exit successfully while individual tests are skipped, excluded or fail. Denylist validation therefore requires the complete structured result, expected subtest inventory and identity of every excluded GPU; the suite-level exit code and a log tail are insufficient.
